body:
Can you reproduce this when using the `canvas_items` stretch mode instead of `viewport`?

Using the `viewport` stretch mode in your example will always render at 1920x1080, even at lower screen resolutions, which is a waste of GPU resources. It will generally look blocky due to nearest-neighbor filtering always being used for `viewport` stretching.

When I switch to `canvas_items` some of my shaders are getting messed up, because they rely on the fact that the viewport size is 1920x1080, and if you switch to `canvas_items` it looks like it will resize all the canvas item nodes to be smaller on the screen, to fit the rendering resolution, right?

I just tried the `canvas_items` stretch mode (updated my shader to just have a fixed resolution instead of getting `SCREEN_TEXTURE_SIZE` to make it work in this mode), and the issue is still reproducible.

Unrelated to all of this, I just noticed on Windows 11 I'm getting strange artifacts, both in my game as well as in the editor - they have not been there before, unsure yet what caused that - might need to file a separate bug.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/da6b6d63-34d9-477e-83bc-cc55028aab32)

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/73924965-585c-4977-8aed-c21aae15e9d9)

which seems to be related to nVidia Vulkan issues: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/102219

> When I switch to `canvas_items` some of my shaders are getting messed up, because they rely on the fact that the viewport size is 1920x1080, and if you switch to `canvas_items` it looks like it will resize all the canvas item nodes to be smaller on the screen, to fit the rendering resolution, right?

I suggest modifying your shaders so that they work regardless of the viewport resolution. Forcing 1920x1080 rendering regardless of window/screen resolution is bound to cause problems later on.

> > When I switch to `canvas_items` some of my shaders are getting messed up, because they rely on the fact that the viewport size is 1920x1080, and if you switch to `canvas_items` it looks like it will resize all the canvas item nodes to be smaller on the screen, to fit the rendering resolution, right?
> 
> I suggest modifying your shaders so that they work regardless of the viewport resolution. Forcing 1920x1080 rendering regardless of window/screen resolution is bound to cause problems later on.

with `viewport` scaling the textures `SCREEN_PIXEL_SIZE` was returning that resolution, with `canvas_items` scaling that value actually gets the the redner resolution, and the canvas items are then scaled down/up to match my target resolution in the Display settings.

Either way, the fact that I want my game to render in that particular resolution has unfortunately nothing to do with the hardware mouse not working properly on Steam Deck. 😄 

So the bug is still valid, and the only fix I found so far is to modify the Steam Deck resolution for my game to match 1920x1080, so that the hardware mouse cursor can go to the bottom right corner.

Long way around alternative is to have the mouse be fully software driven, but that would require more changes to how the user interacts with objects - not impossible, but a workaround, not a fix to the originally raised bug.

Same issue on v4.4.1.stable.official [49a5bc7b6]
Seems like the steam deck cursor displays correctly, but get_global_mouse_position() is returning the wrong position.
Also it will be clipped if you use warp_mouse. 

### Example video:
icon is set to get_global_mouse_position(), steam deck cursor is also visible showing the correct position.
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eed43992-e17b-40fa-986f-4b887f707094

### Reproduction Project:
[steamdeckinputbug.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21108643/steamdeckinputbug.zip)

### Reproduction Steps:
In Project Settings set:
Viewport Width = 512
Viewport Height = 448
Advanced Settings > Viewport Width Override = 1600
Advanced Settings > Viewport Height Override = 1200
Stretch > Mode > viewport

Have a scene where something is set to the mouse's position.

Export for Linux x86_64
upload to steam deck by following these steps: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/steamdeck/loadgames
set Steam Deck controller config to 'Gamepad with Mouse Trackpad'

I have similar issue, although my viewport size is larger than actual screen. Setting viewport to 1920x1080 limits cursor movement to 1280x800 (actual screen size). It isn't distorted (i.e. improper scaling), cursor movement is precise, but it hits 1280 and never moves past that. Same behaviour for `_unhandled_input`, `DisplayServer.mouse_get_position` and so on.

In my shallow debugging I see problem starts with X11 events, as they seems to be in viewport range, but limited to sceeen size (that seems weird. Isn't window size supposed to be the same as actual hardware screen size, and remapping to virtual viewport be done entirely in godot?). What's interesting is if running game without steam (from desktop mode) it works fine (but can't use joysticks for whatever reason). Can't force godot to use wayland implementation to check if it have the same problem.
I had the same issue, then I changed the Window Mode in the Project Parameters from "Windowed" to "Maximized" and it fixed the problem on Steam Deck.

Same problem, and my workaround was to set the window size to 1280x800 in the project settings, and then check at startup whether the game was being run on a Steam Deck or not. If it's not running on Steam Deck, the window resizes to the resolution I want off-deck.
